shots.text: 1666. An apple falls on *Isaac Newton's* head.
Bonk. *Gravity.*
Nope. *Not quite.*
Newton's apple: *the bonk myth.*
The apple part? That's *probably real.*
Newton was at his family farm, hiding from *the plague.*
Years later, he told the story to his friend *William Stukeley.*
He was sitting in the garden, *thinking.*
An apple *fell* from a tree.
And he wondered: why does it always fall *straight down?*
Why not *sideways?* Or *up?*
Maybe the same pull reaches all the way to *the Moon.*
But in Newton's version, *nothing hits his head.*
The bonk was added later, by *storytellers and cartoons.*
And gravity didn't arrive *in a flash.*
He worked on it for about *20 years.*
His big book, the *Principia,* came out in 1687.
And the tree? It's *still growing* at his old house.
Apples that hit Newton on the head: *zero.*
Anyway, here's Newton, getting *bonked.*
